hints: Remember what controls the shape of a Boltzmann curve, temperature controls the spread of molecular energies, while a catalyst only offers a new route.
Since the gas is kept at a constant temperature, think about whether the most probable energy and the height of peak P should change at all.
Now link a catalyst to activation energy, it provides an alternative pathway so the barrier is lowered and more molecules can react.
walkthrough:
**Recall what peak P means**

Think of the curve as showing how energy is shared out between molecules. Peak P marks the most probable energy, and its height and position are fixed by temperature only.

Rule: temperature unchanged means distribution unchanged.

**Recall what a catalyst does**

A catalyst does not heat or cool the mixture and does not change the energies of the molecules. It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.

Effect: $$E_{a}(catalysed) < E_{a}(uncatalysed)$$

**Apply to the diagram**

Because temperature is constant, the whole curve stays exactly where it is, so peak P stays the same height and position. Because $E_{a}$ is smaller, the $E_{a}$ line moves to the left to a lower energy value, so the shaded area to the right gets bigger.

options.A: Incorrect. A lower peak P would mean the distribution has flattened, which only happens when temperature is increased. A catalyst at constant temperature does not change the curve shape.
options.B: Incorrect on both points. Peak P does not drop because temperature is constant, and $E_{a}$ does not move right because a catalyst lowers, not raises, the activation energy.
options.C: Correct. Temperature is constant so the Boltzmann distribution is unchanged and peak P stays the same. The catalyst gives a new route of lower $E_{a}$, so the $E_{a}$ mark moves left and a larger proportion of molecules now have $energy \ge E_{a}$.
options.D: Incorrect. It is right that peak P stays the same, but $E_{a}$ moving to the right would mean a higher barrier and a slower reaction. A catalyst always lowers $E_{a}$, moving it left.
